clue.text: Coins, pieces needed for change

indicators.note: the letters of the word pieces are needed for a change, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is collecting coins because they need loose pieces to give change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for change' is the anagram signal: the letters of PIECES are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Specie is money in the form of coins rather than notes, so it stands for coins.

clue.text: He tamed his darling, game character, with love

parts.note: a darling, someone's favourite, is a pet
RU is rugby union
chi is a Greek letter, a character of that alphabet
love is nil in tennis scoring, written as O

explanation.surface: A man who tamed his sweetheart is described as a playful figure with affection.
explanation.walkthrough: PETRUCHIO is the husband who tames Katharina in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew; the clue's 'his darling' gives PET.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's comedy this suitor is the one who subdues the shrewish Kate, so he is the man who tamed her.

clue.text: Very short examination of a dog

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: A dog gets a very brief check-up from the vet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very short' looks like it describes the examination, but it is the definition; 'examination of a dog' is read literally, the dog first.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtest is the superlative of curt, meaning most brief or abrupt.

clue.text: Member of Greek set a trencherman, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the word for a hearty diner is heard rather than written

parts.note: a trencherman is a big or hearty eater

explanation.surface: A Greek club member is apparently a great eater.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Greek set' is the Greek alphabet, not a social group; EATER spoken sounds like ETA.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet, so one member of that set of letters.

clue.text: Note foreign money may be brass

parts.note: a memo is a written note
the rial is the currency of Iran and other countries

explanation.surface: A note says that foreign currency might turn out to be just brass coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brass' looks like the metal or slang for money, but it means a church brass, an engraved plaque honouring someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A church brass is an engraved metal plate commemorating the dead, so a kind of memorial.

clue.text: Grandma mooches along, giving out yen

indicators.note: giving out means the letter for yen is dropped from the word for strolling

parts.note: to mosey is to mooch or amble along
Y is the abbreviation for yen, the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: An old granny wanders along, handing out Japanese money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving out' takes Y from MOSEYS. Grandma Moses was a celebrated American folk painter who began painting in old age.
explanation.definitionFit: The painter Anna Mary Robertson was known everywhere as Grandma Moses, so her surname follows Grandma.

clue.text: Ceres, say, planting gold tree amid aromatic herb

indicators.note: amid means the gold and tree pieces sit in the middle of the herb

parts.note: mint is an aromatic herb
or is gold in heraldry
the plane is a tree

explanation.surface: A gardener plants a golden tree in the middle of the mint bed, perhaps as an offering to Ceres.
explanation.walkthrough: Ceres looks like the Roman goddess of agriculture, which suits the planting surface, but here it is the dwarf planet in the asteroid belt; 'amid' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceres, the largest body in the asteroid belt, was long classed as an asteroid, which astronomers call a minor planet.

clue.text: Dodges used in game

definitions.meaning: a fast indoor court game played with a ball and racket

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both swindles and a court game related to squash, giving two separate senses.

clue.text: Dock eventually, using maps

indicators.note: to dock is to cut off the tail, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: at last means eventually

explanation.surface: A ship will eventually reach the dock, guided by charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' looks like a harbour, but it means cut the tail off: AT LAST loses its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound book of maps.

clue.text: Leading lady scraps film

parts.note: the leading lady of a show is its star
scraps are fights or wars

explanation.surface: A film's leading actress throws out the script, or gets into fights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scraps' reads as a verb meaning discards, but it is a noun: fights, hence WARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Wars is the 1977 space-opera film by George Lucas.

clue.text: Well, sweet herb's a new starter

indicators.note: the herb's opening letter is swapped for a fresh one, with new giving N

parts.note: sweet cicely is an aromatic herb, so the herb's name is cicely

explanation.surface: Someone says a sweet herb makes a good new first course.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweet cicely is a herb; replace its first letter C with N (new) to get NICELY. 'starter' looks like a first course but means the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicely and well are both adverbs meaning in a satisfactory or pleasing manner.

clue.text: One looks over really big screen

parts.note: super can mean extra large or excellent
a visor is a screen shielding the eyes

explanation.surface: Someone peers over a really big screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One looks over' sounds like a viewer peering over the screen, but it means one who oversees.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervisor oversees work, so is one who looks over what others do.

clue.text: Explorer finding lizard very like fish on top

indicators.note: in a down entry, on top means these pieces come above the lizard

parts.note: as means like
the cod is a fish
the agama is an Old World lizard

explanation.surface: An explorer discovers a lizard that looks rather like a fish from above.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on top' works because this is a down entry: the first three pieces stand above the lizard. Vasco da Gama was the Portuguese navigator who reached India by sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Vasco da Gama was the fifteenth-century Portuguese navigator who opened the sea route to India.

clue.text: Part of bible's not very old language

indicators.note: not means the abbreviation for very is left out of the word for a part of the bible

parts.note: a verse is a numbered part of a chapter of the Bible

explanation.surface: Part of the Bible is written in a language that is not very old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not very old' looks like one phrase, but it splits: 'not very' removes V from VERSE, and 'old language' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: Bird predator finds hard to catch

indicators.note: to catch means the predator holds the letter for hard inside it

parts.note: a cat is a predator
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A bird-hunting predator finds its prey difficult to catch.
explanation.walkthrough: The chat is a small songbird, such as the stonechat or whinchat.
explanation.definitionFit: Chats are small songbirds of the thrush family, such as the stonechat.

clue.text: Aspect of economics team followed with flexibility

indicators.note: followed means the team comes after the flexible piece

parts.note: supply is an adverb form of supple, meaning flexibly
a side is a team

explanation.surface: An economics team carried on in a flexible way.
explanation.walkthrough: The adverb here is the rare one formed from supple, meaning in a supple manner; 'followed' puts the team after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Supply-side economics focuses on boosting production, so it is a branch or aspect of economics.

clue.text: Cooked food in heap left out

indicators.note: out means the letter for left is dropped from the heap

parts.note: a pile is a heap

explanation.surface: Cooked food has been left out in a heap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' reads as one phrase, but 'left' is L and 'out' removes it from PILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie is a baked dish of food in pastry.

clue.text: Sack race: good to enter, to take on record

indicators.note: to take on means the record has the next piece added after it

parts.note: a disc is a record

indicators.note: to enter means the letter for good goes inside the word for race

parts.note: to hare is to run fast or race

explanation.surface: In a sack race, a good competitor enters and then makes the record books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack race' looks like the school sports event, but 'Sack' is the definition and 'race' is HARE, with G entering it.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge someone is to dismiss them from a job, which is what sack means.

clue.text: Type of art ministry got through the back door

indicators.note: got through means the ministry passes inside the door

parts.note: a postern is a back or side door, especially of a castle
MOD is the Ministry of Defence

explanation.surface: An art style was approved by a government department sneaking in through the back door.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ministry of Defence is the UK government department; a postern is an old word for a back gate, and 'got through' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Postmodern art is the style that followed and reacted against modernism.

clue.text: Warder banging up any number during Christmas dinner

indicators.note: during means the number sits inside the Christmas dinner

parts.note: turkey is the traditional British Christmas dinner
N stands for an unspecified number in algebra

explanation.surface: A prison warder locks up any number of inmates while Christmas dinner is served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banging up' (British slang for imprisoning) fits the warder in the surface and supports the containment that 'during' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnkey is an old word for a jailer, someone who keeps the keys of a prison.

clue.text: Not a noble's home?

definitions.meaning: low-born or ignoble, the opposite of noble
home in sports such as baseball, or a home station

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both ignoble and a home position, as in military headquarters or baseball.

clue.text: Trade unionist runs into trouble

indicators.note: into means the letter for runs goes inside the word for trouble

parts.note: bother is trouble
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A trade unionist runs headlong into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Trade unionists traditionally address each other as brother.
explanation.definitionFit: Union members traditionally call one another brother, so a fellow trade unionist is a brother.

clue.text: Beloved daughter, try to do without husband

indicators.note: to do without means the letter for husband is dropped

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court

explanation.surface: A beloved daughter attempts to manage without her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' looks like attempt, but it is the judicial sense: a judge tries or hears a case. HEAR loses H.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear and beloved are both adjectives for someone much loved.

clue.text: Woman sees bishop out of chapel

indicators.note: out of means the letter for bishop is taken from the chapel

parts.note: a bethel is a nonconformist chapel
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A woman sees the bishop leave the chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: A bethel is a nonconformist place of worship; remove B to leave a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethel is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Feature of mason's mark

definitions.meaning: the written word mason's contains this punctuation sign before the s

explanation.definitionFit: It is the punctuation mark seen in the possessive mason's, so it is both a feature of that word and a mark.

clue.text: Enormous limousine bringing one to this ceremony?

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, enormous
a limousine is a car

explanation.surface: A stretch limo brings a star to an awards night.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oscars ceremony is named after its statuette; the question mark flags the loose definition, and the surface is the limousine arrival at the Academy Awards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy Awards ceremony is popularly called the Oscars, after the statuette given to winners.

clue.text: In period of play, unfair bowler's called

indicators.note: called means the bowler's description is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a chucker is a cricket bowler who illegally throws the ball rather than bowling it

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler is called for an unfair delivery during play.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler who throws is a chucker, and 'called' is the umpire's call; the answer, a polo period, sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A chukka is one of the periods of play in a polo match.

clue.text: County game cut payment

indicators.note: cut means the game's name loses its last letter

parts.note: chess is a game
hire is payment for the use of something

explanation.surface: A county council's sports programme had its funding cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the game's final letter before the payment follows. Cheshire is a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheshire is a county in north-west England.

clue.text: Wood found even in Bedlam

indicators.note: even in means the even-numbered letters of the following word are taken

explanation.surface: Wood can be found even in a madhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of Bedlam gives the tree. Bedlam was London's notorious asylum, now meaning chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Elm is a hardwood timber from the elm tree.

clue.text: Critic's unenthusiastic review? Be a sport!

definitions.meaning: a lukewarm verdict on a show would call the play merely fair

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the phrase is a lukewarm theatre verdict, and as an idiom it means behave honourably.

clue.text: People captured cunning little creature

indicators.note: captured means people hold the word for cunning inside

parts.note: men are people
art can mean cunning or craft

explanation.surface: People caught a crafty small animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cunning little creature' looks like one phrase, but 'cunning' gives ART and 'little creature' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The marten is a small weasel-like carnivorous mammal.
